correctness.rationale: The armwise nodal hat Gram matrix and its block Schur complement yield exact inverse entries. Integrating absolute reproducing kernels gives center row 5/3 and leaf row (7S+3ℓ_i)/(3(S+ℓ_i)); convexity plus opposite signs at the central junction excludes interior maximizers. Monotonicity in ℓ_i identifies shortest arms. The fixed-total-length minimax range and norm-two boundary are algebraic consequences with explicit extremizing/limiting configurations. The proof treats arbitrary strictly positive real lengths and m>=3; the extracted standard-library exact rational checker verified 1,982 cases without claiming finite enumeration as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The L∞ norm is the exact worst-case amplification of the globally coupled continuous finite-element L2 projection. Its complete classification over any positive arm-length vector at fixed degree and total length is mathematically natural, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The shortest arm alone governs extremality; equilateral lengths uniquely minimize it; a uniform 7/3 ceiling is sharp but not attained, and degree≥4 forces norm>2 regardless of edge lengths. Norming data and positivity-defect amplitude are explicit, enabling sharp stability and positivity diagnostics at mesh junctions. The result is finite-dimensional in coefficients but analytic in all edge lengths, and goes beyond qualitative one-dimensional bounds.
